data.one_liner: Cross-platform IndexedDB implementation for Dart and Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Provides a browser-compatible IndexedDB API that works on the web (real IndexedDB), Dart VM (IO via sembast), and in-memory for tests. It exposes standard IndexedDB concepts like databases, transactions, object stores, indexes, and key ranges.
use_when: You need structured, transactional storage and indexed queries across multiple platforms including the web.
You want IndexedDB-compatible semantics outside the browser for unit testing your database schema and access.
avoid_when: You prefer an ORM or a simpler key-value/SQL abstraction where you do not want to deal directly with IndexedDB database upgrades and transactions.
strengths: Cross-platform support (Web, Dart VM, mobile, desktop).
Mirrors native IndexedDB semantics allowing easy code sharing.
Provides in-memory factories for fast unit testing.
weaknesses: Requires manual handling of schema migrations inside onUpgradeNeeded callbacks.
IO implementation over Sembast has some limitations compared to native browser IndexedDB.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a lightweight and fast key-value database box without dealing with IndexedDB or SQLite schemas.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer traditional SQLite relational databases for mobile platforms instead of an IndexedDB shim.
